key_insight: Selenium alloying and prolonged air annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOx films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% peak efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improve oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers made by scalable vacuum deposition.
method: Thermally evaporate TeO2:Se powder mixtures at 90:10 wt%.
Anneal films in air at 225 °C for up to 9 hours.
Integrate an 80 nm absorber into ITO/ZnO/TeOx:Se/MoOx/Ag solar cells.
evidence_signal: Optimized devices achieved 0.50 V open-circuit voltage, 8.50 mA/cm² short-circuit current density, a 0.44 fill factor, and photocurrent generation across 300–1000 nm, while residual metallic Te fell to approximately 0.4%.
watch_item: The 9-hour anneal may constrain manufacturing throughput, and the abstract does not report long-term device stability.
paper_title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
